response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.death_state, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hall_of_fame h JOIN player p ON p.player_id = h.player_id GROUP BY p.death_state), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS av FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(c.cnt - a.av) AS avg_above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.cnt > a.av

assumptions.assumption: Representation is the number of hall_of_fame rows per death_state. Every ballot or record counts, so a player with several records counts several times. NULL death_state is its own group.
Only states with at least one Hall of Fame record are in the average. This comes from an inner join between hall_of_fame and player. States with no Hall of Fame records are left out.
The 'average across states' is the unweighted mean of the per-state counts. 'How far above on average' is the mean of (count - that mean) over the states above it.

alternatives.interpretation: Representation is the number of distinct Hall of Fame players per death_state, not the number of records.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.death_state, COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS cnt FROM hall_of_fame h JOIN player p ON p.player_id = h.player_id GROUP BY p.death_state), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS av FROM c) SELECT AVG(c.cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(c.cnt - a.av) AS avg_above_average FROM c CROSS JOIN a WHERE c.cnt > a.av
